title: introduce-ci-sanity-checker-and-graceful-dep-healing
author: Asha Mehta
description:
Motivation and summary:
This PR adds a lightweight CI sanity checker and a 'graceful dependency healer' workflow to reduce noisy broken builds from transitive dependency churn and to catch release-blocking failures earlier in the pipeline. The goal is twofold: (1) run a fast, realistic smoke of critical integration paths immediately in PR context (cache-warmup + a 30s smoke harness) so we fail fast on obvious regressions, and (2) provide automated remediation suggestions (and optionally create quick-fix PRs) for a small class of dependency issues we see most often (semver rollbacks, transient lint/formatting tool drift, and flaky test harness changes).

What this changes (high level):
- .github/workflows/ci-sanity.yml: new lightweight sanity lane that runs on PR open/sync and pre-merge for release branches. It runs a warmup script that primes caches and a short subset of integration smoke tests that exercise serving, the SDK, and the CLI.
- tools/dep-healer/: new small Go service and CLI that implements heuristics for detecting 'recently introduced' failures tied to dependency bumps, attempts safe remediations (pin to previous minor/patch, apply a local patch, or update a tool-compat shim), and can open an automated fix PR with a descriptive body. Runs in lint/dep job as opt-in.
- scripts/ci_warmup.sh & tests/ci/smoke/: warmup and smoke harness artifacts used by ci-sanity lane.
- docs/ci/dep-healing.md: design doc and operator guide for the dep healer runbook and how to opt out or escalate.
- Makefile: new targets for local dev (make ci-sanity, make dep-healer-run).

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- The sanity lane is intentionally conservative: it uses small images, restricted test sets and a short timeout (2m) to avoid adding long waits to PR feedback. It prioritizes deterministic failures (compile, lint, basic e2e) and quick networked checks to catch auth/region regressions.
- Dep-healer is heuristic-driven; it does not auto-merge. By default it opens a 'dep-heal' draft PR; operators can flip a flag in the console to enable auto-apply for low-risk cases. We log every candidate and annotate the original PR with the investigation details.
- We focused the healer on three common patterns from our incidents: toolchain major bumps (formatters/linters), transient semver regressions in transitive deps, and small KV/serialization contract drift that we can patch with a compatibility shim. We intentionally exclude application logic bugs and large dependency upgrades from automated fixes.

Testing and rollout:
- Local: make ci-sanity and make dep-healer-run exercise the same code paths used in CI.
- Staging: the sanity lane was enabled on the staging branch for two weeks; we observed a 27% reduction in noisy CI reruns where the failure was caused by a fresh cache or tool drift.
- Gradual rollout: default behavior is opt-out (not applied to a repo) and will be enabled for core services first. We included a per-repo gate in the action.

Operational notes:
- Observability: the workflow emits a small set of metrics to our observability pipeline: sanity_runs.total, sanity_failures.by_reason, dep_healer.suggestions.total, dep_healer.prs.opened. Dashboards included in docs/ci/dep-healing.md.
- Escalation: healer suggestions are created as draft PRs and tagged "dep-heal"; triage playbook in docs covers when to accept, when to revert, and how to run full test matrix.

Related work and references:
- See ENG-9124 for initial failures analysis that drove this work.
- See ENG-9230 for release gating improvements related to this PR.

Migration instructions:
- No runtime migrations. Repos that want to enable should add a short annotation to their repo config (docs have the snippet) and optionally opt into auto-apply mode.

Notes on implementation scope:
- The PR purposely keeps the healer logic small (~700 lines) and opinionated. If a case requires more complex dependency surgery we route to the platform team via a generated ticket in the PR body.

If you want to run locally: make deps && make ci-sanity || ./tools/dep-healer/dep-healer --dry-run

review_comments: Marcel Dupont (review): Overall looks good. Can we scope the smoke tests so they never hit billable inference units? If not, add a clear whitelist.
Asha Mehta (author): Added a whitelist and mocked serving endpoint for the sanity lane; updated docs to clarify costs.
Priya Nair (review): Dep-healer heuristics look promising, but we should log exact git refs in the suggested PR body so we can audit. Also please add a flag to disable auto-PR creation for org repos.
Asha Mehta (author): Added git ref logging and a per-repo opt-out. Updated action inputs to expose AUTO_PR boolean.
Evan Chou (review): CI timeouts looked tight (2m). Observed one flaky lint flake in staging run. Suggest we add a short retry for known flaky linters instead of expanding timeouts.
Asha Mehta (author): Implemented a 1x retry with jitter for linter step and tightened output capture. Re-ran staging tests.
